text: The Q4 levels for $BTC have held so far. Last month, together with @colin_basco and the @CoinbaseInsto team we put resistance at $87K to $87.8K in our Charting Crypto report. We read the data as near-term consolidation. Price stalled there and ranged below it ever since. A break out of the range is likely to spark significant volatility, although another overhead supply cluster sits around $90k. Read our full quarterly report below 👇 https://twitter.com/glassnode/status/2110737242608246947

ETF buyers came back in size yesterday. US spot $BTC ETFs took in $663M, the most in a day since September, and all of it went into BlackRock's IBIT. That single day erased the funds' net outflows for October. Follow-through would confirm the demand is back.

Short-term profit-taking has weighed on $BTC. Two weeks ago we flagged short-term holders in profit sending the largest share of exchange inflows in a year. This selling has weighed on price since. The flow has now eased back to its average yearly level.

Altcoin leverage is still running hot. Prices have pulled back since leverage peaked earlier this month, yet over 40% of large caps still sit near their highest leverage of the year. In mid caps, that share is at a yearly high. A deeper drop would put many longs at risk.

Bitcoin trades near $82k after a quiet week that held above $80k. The selling behind the early October slide eased, but spot and ETF buyers have not returned, while capital keeps moving into newer hands on-chain. Read the latest Market Pulse 👈

Weekend selling has hit altcoins hard. As fear from equities spills into crypto, the typical altcoin is down over 5%. If the weekend closes like this it would be the largest weekend drop since April. Since the $BTC low in June, buying Friday and selling Sunday was profitable.
